Title_wuva: "We've been blessed': Tuscaloosa County assesses storm damage
Description_wuva: The Tuscaloosa County Emergency Management Agency is assessing the damage caused by Monday's storms. EMA Director Nick Lolley said they began assessing damages Monday from 5:45 p.m. until shortly after 10:30 p.m.Â  The EMA continued assessments Tuesday in areas spanning from Duncanville to Coaling. Storm damages primarily consisted of fallen trees, debris, and extensive power outages. "We've been blessed," Lolley said. So far, only two homes sustained enough damages that residents had to be relocated. One home is in Coaling, where a tree fell on top of the house. The second home is in Duncanville off Alabama Highway 69 South, and also has roof damage from a fallen tree. As the EMA continues storm damage assessments, Lolley said he encourages residents to visit theEMA's websiteand file a report if their property was damaged in Monday's storm. "We need documentation that your home was damaged," Lolley said. Documentation is needed for homeowners filing insurance claims. Documentation also helps identify specifically which weather event caused the damage. "That is only way to get word to the National Weather Service for them to find out if it was straight line winds, a small tornado, anything like that," Lolley said. For those whose property was damaged planning to file an insurance claim, Lolley said you need to submit a report on the website first before filing with your insurance company. The EMA will assess storm damage after a report is filed on the EMA's website. As of Tuesday afternoon, Alabama Power and many other outside contractors were actively working to restore power to the Coaling area. "I think the main thing for our citizens is getting the power back on Highway 11," Lolley said. Damage caused by Monday's storm serves as an important reminder that residents should be weather aware. Here's what you should know long before disaster strikes: If you know severe weather is imminent, stay away from windows and make sure you have at least two ways to get and hear weather warnings. A cellphone and weather radio are ideal. Title_wvtm: Temperatures nearing 90 and the threat of storms increasing soon
Description_wvtm:
Alabama’s hot, humid weather will bring another threat of storms to the state later this week. Temperatures will soar to the 80s and 90s ahead of the return of summertime storms.Check the video forecast for the latest.
We are still about four weeks away from summer’s official start, but the weather is already in summer mode.
Heat and humidity will increase significantly through the rest of this week. Temperatures will rise to the upper 80s and lower 90s on Wednesday, Thursday, and Friday.
The heat index (the apparent temperature to your body) will get into the lower 90s by Friday, and it could get as high as the mid-90s by Sunday.
Short-term rain prospects will be very low, but the chance of daily summer storms will improve through the Memorial Day weekend.
Summer storms and summer heat will be the biggest weather headlines for the upcoming holiday weekend.
Scattered storms will already be in progress late Friday night into Saturday morning over Tennessee and northern Alabama. Those storms will dissipate by midday, but new storms will take their place over Central Alabama through the afternoon.
Any storms that develop could briefly turn severe. That will be true of virtually any thunderstorm over the next few days.
Sunday will be another hot day that feels like the low-mid 90s. Rain chances will be very hit and miss during the afternoon and early evening. There will be many spots that don't see any rain.
Memorial Day looks a little wet, especially over north Alabama. At this point, we don't expect a washout, but plan for rain and thunder at times later in the day. We will be a lot more specific on the exact timing of storms as we get closer to Monday.  Otherwise, the sky is partly cloudy with a high near 90 and a feels like temperature in the low-mid 90s.
If you're traveling south, beach weather looks fantastic! The forecast is hot and dry, with high temperatures reaching the mid to upper 80s. The forecast rip current risk also remains low through the weekend, but always be sure to check your local beach flag for the latest rip current risk.

Title_wvtm: Hot and humid with a few additional storms possible in Alabama through Memorial Day
Description_wvtm:
Heat, humidity, and some storms headline Alabama’s weather through Memorial Day, but next week looks drier.Check the video forecast for the latest.
The first round of storms moved through during the early morning hours producing widespread power outages and trees down across central and north Alabama. Several severe thunderstorm warnings were issued and there was a tornado warning issued at one point to include parts of Cullman county. At one point this morning, there were more than 88,000 people in Alabama without power.
Another round of hit and miss thunderstorms will develop in the afternoon and early evening near and south of Interstate 20. Main threats with these storms are hail, wind and frequent lightning, although it is looking less likely they will have the energy to turn severe. The storm prediction center has removed central Alabama from their severe outlook for this afternoon.
Even if storms are below severe limits, you will need to be alert to storms in the area if you have outdoor plans Monday afternoon and evening. If you can hear thunder you are close enough to the storm to be struck by lightning, even if it is not raining in your location.
Be sure to download the free WVTM app and turn your location on so you can receive real-time lightning alerts.
A weak, cool front will pass through Alabama Monday night, and that will end the threat of rain and storms for an extended time.
The air arriving will be much less sticky and uncomfortable. The humidity will drop, and temperatures fall to the 50s and 60s in the early morning hours by Wednesday and Thursday.
Drier air will hang around through the end of the week suppressing any real threat of significant rain all the way into next weekend.
Rain has been very inconsistent across Alabama over the past month.
Birmingham is almost two inches behind “normal” for May, and we are pushing a 5-inch deficit since March. In other words, we are missing nearly one month of rainfall for the Spring, and that is bad news for summer drought potential.
Long-range forecast guidance suggests that we continue the drier-than-normal trend all the way through June.
The exception to that could be a period of stormy weather starting around June 4 and lasting through June 10. Even that is a “maybe” at this point.
Get ready for some hot, dry days in Alabama as we move into the summer season.

Title_wvtm: Widely scattered storms remain in the forecast Sunday
Description_wvtm:
Mild and muggy for Sunday night. Temperatures climb this week with more summer storms for Central Alabama.Check the video forecast for the latest.
Cloud cover will gradually clear overnight after any remaining storms lose their strength this evening. Calm, yet warm and humid will be the story overnight as temperatures settle in the upper 60s and dew points remain elevated.High pressure builds in on Monday leading to a mostly dry and hot day. Morning clouds and patchy fog will be giving way to some sunshine and a warm afternoon. Temperatures climb into the upper 80s to near 90 degrees, with the feels-like temperatures in the low 90s. It will be plenty humid, so a spotty afternoon storm is possible.
Similar to Monday, Tuesday offers another hot afternoon with highs near 90-degrees and a chance for thunderstorms. Better coverage of those may set up north of I-20 and across the Tennessee Valley.
You can plan for increasing coverage of rain and thunderstorms between Wednesday and Thursday across Central Alabama. The 'threats' will be typical of summer storms with heavy rainfall, frequent lightning, hail, and some strong wind gusts all possible.
The meteorological "ring of fire" will set up and send a few waves of strong storms from the Plains to the South between Tuesday and Thursday.
It's very difficult to time these thunderstorm complexes, but should they make it into Alabama, they can carry a risk of strong to severe winds.
Next weekend does not look like a washout but a chance of storms is almost inevitable this time of year with ample amounts of heat and moisture. That being said, a frontal boundary is expected to sweep across Alabama Friday, briefly dropping the humidity for some.
This will be short-lived. Warm and humid weather will quickly make a return with a slim chance of t-storms Saturday and Sunday. You can anticipate highs in the upper 80s, and a generally sunny sky.
